drug_class: FcRn blocker (neonatal Fc receptor antagonist) with subcutaneous absorption enhancer
purpose: This medicine is used to treat generalized myasthenia gravis, a condition that causes muscle weakness, in adults who have a certain type of antibody called AChR antibody. It is also used to treat a nerve disease called chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP). It helps reduce muscle weakness and improve your ability to do daily activities.
how_it_works: Your immune system makes proteins called antibodies, but in myasthenia gravis and CIDP, some of those antibodies are actually attacking your own body and causing the problem. This medication works by lowering the levels of those harmful antibodies in your blood. It does this by blocking a recycling system in your body that normally keeps antibodies around longer, so the bad antibodies get cleared out more quickly.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include reactions at the injection site such as redness, bruising, or discomfort. You may also notice respiratory infections like a common cold, headache, urinary tract infections, and muscle or joint pain. Some people feel tired or have nausea as well.
warnings: This medicine lowers certain antibody levels, which can increase your risk of infections, so tell your doctor right away if you develop signs of infection like fever, chills, or trouble breathing. Before starting this medicine, make sure your doctor knows if you have any active infections. You should also make sure your vaccinations are up to date before beginning treatment, because this medication may make some vaccines work less well. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given as a shot just under the skin, usually in your belly or thigh. For myasthenia gravis, it is typically given once a week for 4 weeks, and this cycle can be repeated if needed based on how you are doing. Your doctor or nurse will show you or a caregiver how to give the injection at home after proper training.
